recommended.confidence_rule: A 100% letter-for-letter match equals confidence 10 (100%). If one to three letters are off, and those differences are likely suffixes "ing", "ion", "ed", or "er", confidence remains high at 80–85%. After that, confidence of 75% or lower is unacceptable and results in writing unresolved domain. A confidence at or below 0.75 writes unresolved domain.
recommended.method: versioned local associative lexicon; no LLM calls; ranked multi-label evidence; if unresolvable, write unresolved domain; no forced symbol
recommended.rule_module: The actual rules for domain decisions will be an extensive module needing expansion, and will be an entire evening of work one day. For now, the current rule and lists will suffice. If unresolvable, write unresolved domain.
recommended.scoring_rubric: The professional TLD list at https://tld-list.com/tld-categories/professional is primary. If a domain exists on that list, it is domain-specific and tied to that .domain extension; a host of websites therefore exist from which terminology and structures can be extracted easily. If the domain is not part of the professional domain list, fall back to the attached NYCH taxonomy lexicon committed at icm/MG8PK/lexicons/nych-professional-domain-taxonomy.md. That lexicon will be updated with every proper NYCH update.
recommended.seed_lexicon: The professional TLD list at https://tld-list.com/tld-categories/professional is primary. If a domain exists on that list, it is domain-specific and tied to that .domain extension; a host of websites therefore exist from which terminology and structures can be extracted easily. If the domain is not part of the professional domain list, fall back to the attached NYCH taxonomy lexicon committed at icm/MG8PK/lexicons/nych-professional-domain-taxonomy.md. That lexicon will be updated with every proper NYCH update.
recommended.tie_policy: In the strange case of matching — a tie, when two or more domains receive the same score — include both (or all tied domains) and do not prune either domain. Instead use both as possible root domains and reason within both.

recommended.endpoint: The endpoint is the common emoji library. https://unicode.org/emoji/charts/full-emoji-list.html (Unicode Full Emoji List, v18.0). https://www.unicode.org/emoji/charts-18.0/ (Unicode Emoji Charts v18.0).
recommended.inputs: B5 GST and complete natural-language prompt as separate inputs
recommended.request_response_schema:
Symbol selection chooses an emoji/gestalt to represent each word, or compounds multiple words when they form a single idea.

If a compounded idea contains a name, the name-exclusion rule is ignored and the idea is compounded and embedded. Owner example: "fibbonacci sequence" embeds as `FbncSqnc`. The capitalized F indicates a name; the later capitalized S indicates a new word.

In normal gestalt selection, the shortened word is appended at the end of the id string, separated by `_`. Owner example: word becomes `_wrd`. If a second word is compounded to form a single idea, that second word is capitalized. Owner example: "word smith" becomes `wrdSmth`.

The chosen gestalt/emoji should best approximate the gestalt of the word. Owner examples: football = `ftbl` plus the ellipse-on-an-angle football emoji; hammer uses the hammer emoji. This will not always produce the most obvious gestalt; the word embedding gives enough of a clue to negate collisions and provide context by observing neighboring gestalt IDs.

A legend is printed atop the chat for domain-tree symbol mappings, because there are far more domains than emoji and unique choices cannot exist in an invariant lexicon. The current domain is identified and all subdomains are preserved. Gestalts as emoji are chosen according to the current domain. If the domain is switched, a marker is placed for indexing and the new legend is transmitted.

Invariants that never change per prompt or chat, and are universal to all NYCH uses and users, must be canonized in these contract terms: modality operators; narrative perspective and tense; time of day if any; and the grammatical invariants.

Everything that is not invariant is domain-selected. Unrelated domains are pruned until they are referenced by chat or inferred by actions.

At the point the LLM call is made to choose the gestalt emoji, NYCH symbols are chosen per word. This happens after the domain has been identified and the lookup has given subdomains and related structure. Those symbols are temporary or unique to this chat. They will eventually become normalized because of the legend and the LLM preference for stability. Per domain there will not be much variance, but some domains will require the same symbols. For example, computers and word processing may both use the computer-screen gestalt as the best match, and that symbol will represent something different in each domain. That on-the-fly sharing is the reason for choosing symbols this way.
recommended.tote_write_policy:
The modality operator is invariant and symbolic, but the TOTE loop database is inherently not symbolic, because symbols are chosen by domain. The TOTE loop library is the words organized in cells, rows, and columns: domain-specific, subdomain, and technique. Then the TOTE loop describes the technique with a minimum of 1 actor, 1 action, 1 object, and 1 modality operator.

Word organizing in the database will preserve the domain organization and the TOTE loop sequence, and allow all but the modality operators to be dynamically chosen.

recommended.abbreviation_to_gestalt_training: Part of training this model is training from word abbreviations to stabilized gestalt dynamics. This is unique to the NYCH language model.
recommended.attention_mixture: Attention weights the current ID and its neighbors as follows, as a starting mix: 30% the current gestalt, 30% the current abbreviated word, 20% neighboring gestalts, and 20% neighboring abbreviated words (the remaining 40% neighboring signal split 20/20). If that mix does not work, readjust the percentages and ratios. Adjust until optimal percentages and ratios are obtained through testing on natural language ("nat lang"). The 30% current gestalt / 30% current abbreviated word / 20% neighboring gestalts / 20% neighboring abbreviated words mix is the starting point, not a frozen optimum.
recommended.primacy_tradeoff: Until patterns are recognized from repetition, the abbreviated words appended on the gestalt ID string are primary. A tradeoff rule determines when the dynamic domain lexicons have stabilized; only then may the switch to symbolic (gestalt) primary be made. Words are not discarded; they remain appended on the ID string.

recommended.mixing_console: A dynamic mixing console adjusts these numbers in real time like an audio mixer and finds the intended balance. An AI may perform the mixing under human observation. The console does not have to be used to obtain the live parameters at first. The mix channels being balanced are the current gestalt, the current abbreviated word, neighboring gestalts, and neighboring abbreviated words, starting from the D8 mix of 30/30/20/20, plus the D9 block numbers (especially feed-forward width and training dropout) that affect how those signals are mixed. Inference dropout remains 0.0 and is not a mix channel.
recommended.repeatability: The console must produce repeatable outcomes. The same recipe — operator (human or AI observed), observation seed, mix-channel values, and D9 block settings — must yield the same mix and the same digest, and the same seed plus starting mix must replay the same observed AI moves.

recommended.verification_sidecar: The production D10 path still scores next NYCH tokens — gestalt IDs with the abbreviated word appended on the ID string — not full English words. To be sure that path is working, a parallel unmodified ("standard") version must ride the whole process alongside the abbreviated-word and gestalt mix as a faithfulness check. The mixed NYCH path should remain faithful if it is running alongside that proper unmodified companion. Once the D10 step is proven, delete the standard version. This sidecar is required verification, not an optional extra: it exists so the mixed path can be checked before it is trusted on its own.

recommended.memory_latency_target: Reference-derived recommendation from Eldan and Li, TinyStories (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07759. Float32 weights are 4 bytes per parameter: 7219712 bytes at 1804928 parameters and 27831296 bytes at 6957824 parameters. A float32 Adam training lower bound, excluding activations, is 16 bytes per parameter (weights, gradient, first moment, and second moment): 28878848 bytes and 111325184 bytes at those ends. Activation bytes are not capped here. The paper does not publish a millisecond latency, and D8 records no KV cache in the reference, so this is not a cached-decode budget. The wall-clock class is the one the paper states for models of about 1M to 35M parameters and 1 to 8 layers: training on a single V100 in at most 30 hours. This is a reference-derived starting budget for owner review.
recommended.parameter_band: Reference-derived recommendation from Ronen Eldan and Yuanzhi Li, TinyStories (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07759. This is not a copy of their GPT-Neo checkpoint. The approved NYCH shape stays d_model 128, 2 layers, 4 heads, head width 32, SwiGLU width 512, RoPE, position limit 1024, float32, and tied embeddings. Non-embedding count assumes no linear bias, RMSNorm scale only, one pre-norm on attention and one on SwiGLU in each layer, one final RMSNorm, and zero RoPE parameters: 2*(4*128*128 + 3*128*512 + 2*128)+128 = 524928. Vocabulary size is not frozen. The band uses the two vocab sizes that source states: 10000 (paper footnote: keep the top 10K GPT-Neo tokens) and 50257 (vocab_size in the TinyStories-1M and TinyStories-2Layers-33M config.json files at https://huggingface.co/roneneldan/TinyStories-1M/raw/main/config.json and https://huggingface.co/roneneldan/TinyStories-2Layers-33M/raw/main/config.json). Tied embeddings add 128*V once, so the band is 1804928 parameters at V=10000 and 6957824 parameters at V=50257. This is a reference-derived size band for owner review, not a claim that NYCH uses the GPT-Neo vocabulary.
recommended.training_hardware: Reference-derived recommendation: one NVIDIA V100 GPU. Eldan and Li, TinyStories (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07759, state that their models in the roughly 1M to 35M parameter range, with 1 to 8 layers, can all be trained on a single V100 within at most 30 hours, and that this training is typically less than a day on a single GPU. The computed NYCH band, 1804928 to 6957824 parameters, sits inside that range. This records no measured NYCH training run.

recommended.gestalt_id_abbreviation: Owner-stated answer from Nick Hartman. Not an approval. Verbatim: "drop vowels and double consonants keep y and capitalize if compound with a name like Fibonacci sequence gets FbncSqnc or compounded without name gets brick layer to brkLyr or computer programmer to cmptrPrgrmr". Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: drop a, e, i, o, u; keep y; collapse identical letters. Stored on pending D15. The helper is not wired into any Builder. Owner clarification, verbatim in full: "just dont drop the c and modOp is better and (object_k) can be (obj_k) but yes it could be (obj_bmp=gst) (obj_k=gst)". c stays, so brick layer is brckLyr. Owner clarification, verbatim: "any word that starts with a vowel gets an ' and if it starts with a vowel and that vowel is followed by a double dont drop the double so apple = 'ppl that distinguishes it from opal = 'pl". apple is 'ppl and opal is 'pl. Owner example, verbatim: "fried apple  fryd"ppl". Owner answer on that y, verbatim: "yes i thought about it and sometimes it just makes sense to preserve the sound and not introduce vowels by using a y". Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: a y may be used to preserve a vowel sound without introducing vowels. It is discretionary ("sometimes"), so it is not a general algorithmic rule. An earlier join wrote fried apple as fryd"ppl. Owner clarification, verbatim: "do it when a hard vowel like capital I sound is needed and for like eye 'y' it makes it distinct to use the ' as an annotaion of vowel sound but not use the vowel". Owner clarification, verbatim: "i before e except after c  fried   died usually the ie is a hard I sound". Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: the letter sequence ie is written as y before the normal vowel-drop, so fried is fryd and died is dyd. Exceptions are owner-only.  Owner statement, verbatim: "feeld peece frend scyence those are the phonetics but reallly fld p''c so change the rule from fryd"ppl to fryd'Ppl and then the double " is a marker for two consonants in a row anywhere". Owner correction, verbatim: " denotes that there are two vowels in a row here not always or exclusively the same vowels just that there is two". That correction supersedes the two-consonants wording. Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: p''c means p"c, so piece is p"c. A vowel-initial later part keeps its leading ' and is capitalized, so fried apple is fryd'Ppl, superseding fryd"ppl. Owner confirmation, verbatim: "yes f"ld is correct". field is f"ld. field is f"ld and piece is p"c. The " marker is not a general default. friend and science have no abbreviation.  Owner rule, verbatim: "one rule i had a while ago was no word of three letters or less is worth symbolizing or shortening". Owner follow-up, verbatim: "no dont shorten eye i just came back up with the no shorten at 3 or below". A standalone word of three letters or fewer stays as written, so eye stays eye. Owner example, verbatim: "hot dog can be htDg". Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: the limit is for standalone words only. Compound parts are still abbreviated in camelCase, so hot dog is htDg.  Owner criterion, verbatim: "if the adjective is imperative to the noun as an object it gets compounded meaning if the gestalt is lost without the adjective then the adjective and noun are a noun together its an object hot dog is lost without both words and must be compounded." Compound only when the gestalt is lost without the adjective. This is not detectable from spelling. Only owner-listed pairs are compounded. hot dog is the pair given under this criterion.  Owner rationale, verbatim: "that way if we are talking about a hot dog  as in the dog is hot it can be understood distinctly with out collision". Literal hot dog stays separate words. Compound htDg is the food, so they do not collide. Open: obj_k; double-keep scope; longer y-initial and all-vowel words; a single proper-name word; hyphenated compounds; compounds of 3 or more parts; a vowel-initial first part.
recommended.interlinear_annotation:
Owner-stated answer from Nick Hartman. Not an approval. Verbatim: "what I would like is a sort of info tree to exist interlinear so before gestalts are picked the nych output is still words but the info exists above in a sub-line interlinear style." Example given:
(domain=building_subdom=carpentry)(modalityOp=kine-int)(past-t)
the carpenter                                               freaked  out           after               he took the bump of k.
Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: words stay on the base line and tags sit above them. Span alignment, the tense source, and persistence after gestalt selection stay open. Stored on pending D15 because approved D10 text was not edited. Owner addendum, confirmed: "he took the bump of k" also gets tags. Verbatim example:
(pronoun)(modOp=kine-ext)(object=gestalt)(object_k=gestalt)
he took the bump of k
Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: "he" maps to (pronoun); "took" maps to (modOp=kine-ext); "the bump" maps to (object=gestalt); "k" maps to (object_k=gestalt). The full sentence above remains the first interlinear test fixture (nych_preview/fixtures/interlinear_examples.json, entry full-sentence). Open and not decided: the exact span alignment of each tag on the full sentence; the tag syntax grammar; whether tense is an existing modality operator or a new tag type; whether the interlinear line persists after gestalts are picked. Owner clarification, verbatim: "just dont drop the c and modOp is better and (object_k) can be (obj_k) but yes it could be (obj_bmp=gst) (obj_k=gst)". Canonical modality tag key is modOp. The carpenter fixture's original verbatim text used modalityOp and is kept unchanged. Normalized form of that fixture, using modOp, is:
(domain=building_subdom=carpentry)(modOp=kine-int)(past-t)
the carpenter                                               freaked  out           after               he took the bump of k.
Object tags are owner-confirmed: the key prefix is obj_ followed by the object's abbreviated surface token, and the value gst means gestalt. For example, (obj_bmp=gst) for "the bump" and (obj_k=gst) for "k". Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: bmp is the consonant skeleton of bump, and gst abbreviates gestalt. Normalized form of "he took the bump of k":
(pronoun)(modOp=kine-ext)(obj_bmp=gst)(obj_k=gst)
he took the bump of k
Owner statement, verbatim: "domains will switch globally and inter sentence structurally many times and thats why an invariant tag for domain or subdomain switch can be helpful just to indicate whether its a temporary switch like in subject for a  sentence and overall topic domain global for a chat". An invariant tag marks a domain or subdomain switch: temporary within a sentence, or global for the chat. Interpretation, flagged as interpretation: that scope separates htDg the food from the words hot dog. Owner spelling, verbatim: "dom><folloowed by a token number or dom><global". Owner clarification, verbatim: "temp is dom>12 and lands interlinear where it occurs and the number is for tokens from that point". Owner statement, verbatim: "dom>?=food and after however many tokens the domain switches back or to something else the tag ?=12  where ? is any variable like x or z". Interpretation, flagged as interpretation and not owner-confirmed: this supersedes dom>N. It opens as dom>x=food. The writer picks the variable, such as x or z, and the value after = names the domain. Where the switch ends, the same variable closes it as x=12, the token count. Global stays dom><global. (dom_sw=tmp) and (dom_sw=glb) stay superseded. Open: whether the closing tag sits where the switch ends and 12 counts back to the opening tag; whether the domain reverts automatically there; how dom><global names its domain, such as dom><global=food; whether different variables nest or overlap; and parentheses around the tag.

decisions.rationale: Owner approved the catalog v3.26 recommendation for D16. The same verbatim statement approved D12, D13, D14, and D16 together. Items labeled interpreted stay interpreted. Open questions remain unresolved.

recommended.format: Reference-derived recommendation: a private versioned package with float32 weights and a JSON config recording the approved NYCH shape (d_model 128, 2 layers, 4 heads, head width 32, SwiGLU width 512, RoPE, position limit 1024, tied embeddings), the actual vocabulary size, the parameter-count assumptions, and the catalog digest. The float32 dtype follows the TinyStories checkpoints whose config.json sets torch_dtype to float32: https://huggingface.co/roneneldan/TinyStories-1M/raw/main/config.json and https://huggingface.co/roneneldan/TinyStories-2Layers-33M/raw/main/config.json, from Eldan and Li, TinyStories (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07759. The package is not a GPT-Neo checkpoint. Visibility stays private_until_explicit_release.
recommended.runtime_device: Reference-derived recommendation: train and evaluate the float32 reference on one NVIDIA V100-class GPU. Eldan and Li, TinyStories (2023), https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.07759, trained the roughly 1M to 35M parameter models on a single V100 in at most 30 hours. Inference in this recommendation adds no KV cache, consistent with the approved D8 reference. This is a reference-derived device class for owner review, not a measured NYCH run. Visibility stays private_until_explicit_release.
